header.title: Welcome to pmMDA - poor man's Model Driven Architecture -

section.title: Introduction
section.p: The pmMDA – poor man MDA - tool is a pragmatic approach to apply MDA approach in commercial and industrial projects. Tedious source artifacts are generated from a model instead of being hand-coded. Talented developers should concentrate on application design and not on writing repetitive code. Currently pmMDA provides extensive support for Java client/server applications using JDBC – meaning 2 tiers programs -. CORBA and J2EE middleware - meaning 3 tiers programs - are also supported. Related projects provides code generator for the .NET environment. Work is under way to support C++ based applications.

The goal is to provide a tool empowering designers to specify a MDA model, validate it and generate the source code to execute it. Commercial applications are the major scope of the project. In a second phase industrial products are supported.

pmMDA reads UML models, e.g. from ArgoUML tool, extends them with tagged values and generates the source code and configuration artifacts for the target applications. The tagged values are described in the user manual and are legal extensions to the UML method. Therefore the models can still be edited with UML tools. The pmMDA provides a user interface simplifying the edition and validation of tagged values.

The MDA approach becomes powerful when available frameworks provides powerful abstraction to progam against. The pmMDA project provides a set of complete frameworks streamlining client server program development.

section.title: How to use it?

ul.li: Describe your domain model with ArgoUML. The full power of UML is available. The domain model can contains packages, classes, interfaces, attributes and relationships.

Start pmMDA and read your model. Edit the tagged values in the user interface, run the validation to verify that your model is complete. Sophisticated support for bidirectional relations, vetoable and changeable properties is provided through specialized cartriges.
Generate the source code artifacts of your application, compile them and run your application.
Iterate to add new features in your model.

section.p: The examples in the distribution provide complete ArgoUML UML models with configured tagged values, the pmMDA properties file to generate the code artifacts and an ant script to compile it.

A two minutes tutorial is available under
two minutes pmMDA tutorial
. The provided example runs as two tiers application, as three tiers CORBA and as three tiers J2EE client/server programs.

A slightly longer
five minutes pmMDA tutorial
creates a functional PIM LDIF2VCARD translator. This application can be used to transfer your Thunderbird address book into a iPod compatible contact book. Now you can use your iPod as PDA to access your contacts and calendar.

section.title: Resources
section.p: The pmMDA provides the following sets of resources.
pmMDA engine defining the metamodel to describe your application and the execution engine executing the cartridges. The model can be defined in a UML such ArgoUML and imported in pmMDA .
A set of cartridges generating the source code and configuration artifacts to run the application. The cartridges are written in Java. The generation template uses the Jakarta Velocity project.
section.note: The cartridges generate rich client application as two tiers clients, or clients connected to CORBA servers or J2EE servers.
section.p: Frameworks simplifying the development of complex mission-critical applications. One of the provided framework implements a data object graph manipulation framework and persistence. We are looking at JSR-235 to standardize this approach. The persistence is realized using the Apache OJB project. A second framework provides a explorer framework to visualize and manipulate graphs of objects using the tree list paradigm.
section.note: Powerful explorer based interface, complete persistence layer and application framework are available. Each framework can be introduced in applications without using the pmMDA .

section.title: Documentation
section.p: Each subproject has its own set of documentation and tutorials. The public interfaces and methods are described in the API documentation generated with JavaDoc.
A seperate section of the site provides articles and presentations about design and implementation aspects of the subprojects.

section.title: Quality and Metrics
section.p: Quality metrics are provided for all hosted projects. The pmMDA group adheres to the agile process philosophy. Release often, do not wait until it is perfect. But in the long term the quality of the source code and documentation should pass all defined and agreed quality criteria. The group provides metrics for all source code and documentation artifacts of the project.
